title: A Podcast on Changing Careers Through Night Classes
script: Host: [thoughtful] Today's guest spent eleven years as an accountant before retraining as a nurse. Thanks for joining me, Ratna.
Host: What made you consider such a drastic change after over a decade in one field?
Guest: [carefully] Honestly, I'd grown comfortable, but comfort had started to feel indistinguishable from boredom, if that makes sense.
Host: It does. Was there a specific moment that pushed you toward nursing, though, rather than just general dissatisfaction?
Guest: [reflective] A family hospital experience motivated me, but I protect my father’s medical privacy. Inspiration did not establish my suitability or competence.
Host: Even though that experience moved you emotionally, retraining still required years of night classes. How did you manage both?

Guest: [honestly] Before enrolling, I checked accredited education, entry, clinical placement, licensing, cost, schedule, health, background, care, and support requirements. The workload still required adjustment.
Host: Did you ever consider quitting the program once you started?
Guest: [seriously] Constantly, particularly during exam weeks, when I questioned whether starting over at thirty-four was reckless rather than brave.
Host: What convinced you to continue despite those doubts?
Guest: [gently] A classmate reminded me that in five years, that time would pass regardless, whether or not I finished the program.
Host: That's a compelling way to think about it. Did your accounting background turn out useless in nursing?
Guest: [encouraging] Attention to detail transferred, but accounting did not replace supervised clinical learning, patient safety, communication, or formal competence assessment.
Host: How did your family react to the decision initially?
Guest: [sincere] My husband supported me immediately, whereas my mother worried I was throwing away years of seniority for uncertainty.
Host: What would you tell someone considering a similar leap right now?
Guest: [thoughtful] Investigate the regulated pathway, finances, care, health, aptitude, and alternatives. Discomfort and outcomes vary; no story guarantees qualification or employment.
Host: Beautifully put, Ratna. Thank you for sharing your story with us today.
Guest: [carefully] Thank you for having me. I hope it nudges someone off the fence they've been sitting on.
